---
title: "Using Q-CRAFT from Python"
subtitle: "Long-term fiscal risk under climate scenarios"
resources: [../assets/graph/**]
---

Q-CRAFT turns a named set of macro-fiscal and climate assumptions into
reproducible paths for GDP, balances, and debt through 2099. Teal Insights
publishes this Python package; the tool and its underlying guidance note are
from the IMF. This publication does not imply IMF endorsement.

The [worked assessment](01-worked-assessment.qmd) shows the economic result
first: for one France assumption set, rigid primary expenditure produces a
2099 debt ratio of about 125 percent of GDP under Paris and 251 percent under
Hot unadapted. The [methodology guide](02-methodology-and-interpretation.qmd)
explains what those comparisons do and do not measure.

## Install

```bash
uv add "qcraft-2024-11-15 @ git+https://github.com/Teal-Insights/qcraft-2024-11-15"
```

## Start here

1. [Run the worked assessment](01-worked-assessment.qmd).
2. [Interpret the identities and scenario conventions](02-methodology-and-interpretation.qmd).
3. Browse the generated [API reference](../reference/index.qmd).

Q-CRAFT is a partial-equilibrium, stylized long-term assessment. It does not
model adaptation spending, natural-disaster GDP losses, sea-level rise,
monetary conditions, financing constraints, or the GDP effect of fiscal
adjustment. Use it alongside country-specific macro-fiscal and climate models.
